claims.text: Hand-parsed because tomllib landed in 3.11 and this package targets 3.10 with zero runtime dependencies.
claims.why: The code uses regex and manual parsing without importing tomllib; claim matches implementation.

claims.text: ``elif cmd == "spawn": _spawn(rest)`` puts the real imports one hop away, in a module-local helper. Without the closure that whole subcommand's targets are invisible.
claims.why: The comment references a specific code pattern not present in this chunk; the function itself computes transitive calls, but the example is not verifiable.

claims.text: Any edge it has that this walk does not is REPORTED in ``index_extra_edges`` and is NOT added to the graph: structcore resolves imports without branch context, so unioning its edges back in re-admitted exactly the ``if False:`` and swallowed- ``ImportError`` imports this engine refuses on purpose, and printed the target ``reachable``.
claims.why: The claim references index_extra_edges and structcore behavior; neither is present in this chunk. The code shows index parameter but not its processing.

claims.text: A disagreement between the two engines is a finding, not a discovery, and a finding may not quietly promote a module.
claims.why: No code in this chunk handles disagreements or promotion; references behavior outside chunk.

claims.text: Resolved exactly like real ones, then kept OUT of ``edges``. They exist only to answer "why is this module here at all", so an unreached module somebody clearly intended to load is ``unknown`` rather than an island.
claims.why: The comment describes intent, but the actual weak_edges list is only initialized; no resolution or usage is shown in this chunk.

observations.what: _console_scripts uses hand-parsed TOML, which may miss edge cases like inline comments or multi-line values.
analyse function builds explicit edges and weak_edges list but does not show usage of index or weak_edges processing.
_func_closure uses src.func_records and src.func_calls; these are expected to be populated by _scan not shown in this chunk.
